title: Berlin Election 2026 - Quick Summary
items: **Sunday 20 September 2026, polls open 8:00 to 18:00.** Berlin elects the Abgeordnetenhaus and the twelve district assemblies (BVV). There is **no referendum**: both spring initiatives fell short of their signature targets and were declared failed on 22 May.

**Your passport decides the sheets.** German citizens get the Abgeordnetenhaus paper with **two votes** plus the BVV paper with **one**. Citizens of another EU country get the **BVV paper only**, about **250,000** people. Any other passport gets no ballot this time.

**Two more conditions for everyone:** born before **21 September 2010**, so 16 on election day, and a main home in Berlin since **20 June 2026** at the latest. About 55,000 16 and 17 year olds vote for the state parliament for the first time.

**One combined ballot paper now.** First vote for a constituency candidate on the left, second vote for a party list on the right, the way the Bundestag ballot works. The BVV sheet is separate and has two punched holes so you can tell it apart by touch.

**The postal vote clock:** online application until **Tuesday 15 September**, written application or a walk-in vote at the Briefwahlstelle until **Friday 18 September, 15:00**, a replacement Wahlschein until **Saturday 12:00**, and the red envelope physically at the Bezirkswahlamt by **Sunday 18:00**. Allow three working days by post.

**Bring photo ID on Sunday**, even an expired one. The notice is helpful, not required; the Wahllokalsuche finds your station from your address. Nobody can vote in your place, and once you hold a Wahlschein you cannot vote without it.
